visualReview.conclusion: Rebinding the original renderer did not restore visibility in this observed state. Only the original-surface capture after associating the auxiliary renderer was visible; this side effect does not validate keeping an unused renderer, persistence after detachment, normal cold startup or production UI.

causalBoundaries: Removing projectedShadow disables both the pre-SceneKit source shadow-map stage and the post-SceneKit receiver/Gamma stage; A/B cannot isolate only the map.
Existing projected-shadow code ends each independent encoder; no source evidence establishes a Metal encoder-state leak.
A, B and C have identical opaque-black bytes; rebinding the original renderer did not recover this state. This does not establish a universal statement about all renderer initialization sequences.

D became visible while the same original surface performed capture after one auxiliary renderer association. No render, prepare or snapshot was requested from that fresh renderer; the exact framework mechanism remains unproven.

The fresh renderer was unbound and this test strong reference cleared after D. ARC deallocation and visibility after detachment were not observed, and keeping an unused fresh renderer is not a validated production fix.

The test made one explicit draw; the normal submission counter was observed as zero before the experiment and one after that draw. This does not erase the World constructor drawState call or turn offscreen captures into live UI acceptance.
remaining: Use the authenticated A/B/C-black, D-visible evidence to assess a minimal production registration/initialization fix without adding an unused permanent auxiliary renderer.
Any candidate still requires actual verification of the normal cold first frame with the original projector; no current production fix is claimed.
Keep live UI, audible audio, performance and physical-device acceptance as separate outstanding scopes; do not repeat successful historical methods or upload the same resource version.
